results.title: Finite residue field of a completed number ring
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a number field and $v$ a nonzero prime ideal of its ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_K$. The residue field of the ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_v$ of the $v$-adic completion $K_v$ of $K$ is finite.

results.title: Compactness of the completed ring of integers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a number field and $v$ a nonzero prime ideal of its ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_K$. The ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_v$ of the $v$-adic completion $K_v$ of $K$ is a compact subset of $K_v$.

results.title: Diagonal map into the ideles
results.caption: Definition

results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Norm-one ideles
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $K$ be a number field. The norm-one ideles of $K$ form the kernel of the adelic norm, the subgroup of the topological idele group of $K$ (with $R = \mathcal{O}_K$) consisting of the ideles whose adelic norm is $1$.

results.title: Membership in the norm-one ideles
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a number field. An idele $a$ of $K$ (with $R = \mathcal{O}_K$) lies in the subgroup of norm-one ideles if and only if its adelic norm is $1$.

results.title: Product formula for principal ideles
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a number field. For every $x \in K^\times$, the principal idele of $x$ (its image under the diagonal embedding of $K^\times$ into the topological idele group, with $R = \mathcal{O}_K$) has adelic norm $1$.

results.title: Principal ideles have norm one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a number field. The subgroup of principal ideles of $K$ (with $R = \mathcal{O}_K$) is contained in the subgroup of norm-one ideles; that is, every principal idele has adelic norm $1$.

results.title: Principal ideles of norm one
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a number field $K$, this is the subgroup of the group $I_K^1$ of ideles of $K$ with adelic norm $1$ consisting of the principal ideles, that is, of the elements of $I_K^1$ that are images of elements of $K^\times$ under the diagonal embedding.

results.title: Norm-one idele class group
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: For a number field $K$, the norm-one idele class group $C_K^1 = I_K^1 / K^\times$ is the quotient of the group $I_K^1$ of ideles of $K$ with adelic norm $1$ by its subgroup of principal ideles, the images of the elements of $K^\times$ under the diagonal embedding.

results.title: Principal ideles are trivial in the norm-one idele class group
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a number field. For every $x \in K^\times$, the principal idele of $x$, viewed as an element of the group $I_K^1$ of ideles of $K$ with adelic norm $1$, has trivial class in the norm-one idele class group $C_K^1 = I_K^1 / K^\times$.

results.title: The principal ideles are discrete
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a number field $K$, the subgroup of principal ideles is discrete in the idele group of $K$, where the idele group carries the product of the product topology at the infinite places and the restricted-product topology at the finite places.

results.title: Generating function of the Genocchi numbers
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The Genocchi power series is the formal power series $\frac{2x}{e^x + 1} = 2x \cdot (e^x + 1)^{-1}$ in $\mathbb{Q}[[x]]$, where $e^x = \sum_{n \ge 0} x^n / n!$ is the exponential power series and $(e^x + 1)^{-1}$ is the inverse of $e^x + 1$ among formal power series. It is the exponential generating function of the Genocchi numbers $G_n$, that is, $\frac{2x}{e^x + 1} = \sum_{n \ge 0} G_n \frac{x^n}{n!}$.

results.title: Genocchi numbers
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, the Genocchi number $G_n \in \mathbb{Q}$ is $n!$ times the coefficient of $x^n$ in the Genocchi power series $\frac{2x}{e^x + 1} \in \mathbb{Q}[[x]]$, so that $\frac{2x}{e^x + 1} = \sum_{n \ge 0} G_n \frac{x^n}{n!}$.

results.title: The Genocchi power series is $2x/(e^x + 1)$

results.title: Genocchi numbers from their generating function
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$, the Genocchi number $G_n$ equals $n!$ times the coefficient of $x^n$ in the Genocchi power series $\frac{2x}{e^x + 1} \in \mathbb{Q}[[x]]$.

results.title: Genocchi numbers in terms of Bernoulli numbers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$, the Genocchi number $G_n$, defined by $\frac{2x}{e^x + 1} = \sum_{m \ge 0} G_m \frac{x^m}{m!}$, satisfies $G_n = 2(1 - 2^n) B_n$, where $B_n$ is the $n$-th Bernoulli number with the convention $B_1 = -\tfrac{1}{2}$.

results.title: The two definitions of the Genocchi numbers agree
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$, the rational number $2(1 - 2^n) B_n$, where $B_n$ is the $n$-th Bernoulli number with the convention $B_1 = -\tfrac{1}{2}$, equals the Genocchi number $G_n$ defined by the exponential generating function $\frac{2x}{e^x + 1} = \sum_{m \ge 0} G_m \frac{x^m}{m!}$.

results.title: Height of a lattice path
results.caption: Definition

results.title: Height of a sequence of Dyck steps
results.caption: Definition

results.title: $k$-Dyck path
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $n$ and $k$ be natural numbers. A lattice path of $2n$ steps, each an Up step $(1, 1)$ or a Down step $(1, -1)$, is a $k$-Dyck path of semilength $n$ if its height after all $2n$ steps is $0$, its height after its first $j$ steps is at least $-k$ for every $j \le 2n$, and, when $n \ge 1$, its last step is a Down step.

results.title: Running a program on a binary string
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a code $c$ of a partial recursive function on the natural numbers and a binary string $w$, running $c$ on $w$ evaluates $c$ at the number encoding $w$; if this halts with output $m$, the result is the binary string encoded by $m$. The result is undefined when the evaluation does not halt or $m$ encodes no binary string.

results.title: Description of a code running on an input
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $c$ be a code for a partial recursive function and let $n$ be its number in the standard encoding of codes as natural numbers. For a binary string $w$, the description of $c$ running on $w$ is the binary string $1^n 0 w$, that is, $n$ ones, then a zero, then $w$.

results.title: The universal description method
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A description `1ⁿ 0 w` runs code number `n` on `w`; a string of `1`s describes nothing.

results.title: Kolmogorov complexity
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The Kolmogorov complexity $K(x)$ of a binary string $x$ is the least length of a binary string $p$ such that $U(p)$ is defined and equals $x$, where $U$ is the universal description method.

results.title: A description bounds the complexity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $x$ and $p$ be binary strings such that $U(p)$ is defined and equals $x$, where $U$ is the universal description method. Then the Kolmogorov complexity of $x$ is at most the length of $p$: $K(x) \le |p|$.

results.title: Shortest descriptions exist
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every binary string $x$ there is a binary string $p$ whose length is the Kolmogorov complexity $K(x)$ and such that $U(p)$ is defined and equals $x$, where $U$ is the universal description method.

results.title: Complexity is at most the length plus a constant
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There is a natural number $c$ such that every binary string $x$ satisfies $K(x) \le |x| + c$, where $K(x)$ is the Kolmogorov complexity of $x$ and $|x|$ is its length.

results.title: The universal description method is partial recursive
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The universal description method, as a partial function from binary strings to binary strings, is partial recursive.

results.title: Every partial recursive description method has a code
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $D$ be a partial recursive function from binary strings to binary strings. Then there is a code $c$ for a partial recursive function such that running $c$ equals $D$ as a partial function: for every binary string $w$, running $c$ on $w$ is defined exactly when $D(w)$ is, and then has the same value.

results.title: Optimality (the invariance theorem)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $D$ be a partial recursive function from binary strings to binary strings, viewed as a description method. Then there is a natural number $c$ such that for all binary strings $x$ and $p$ for which $D(p)$ is defined and equals $x$, the Kolmogorov complexity of $x$ satisfies $K(x) \le |p| + c$, where $|p|$ is the length of $p$.

results.title: Doubling costs a constant
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There is a natural number $c$ such that for every binary string $x$, the Kolmogorov complexity of the concatenation $xx$ of $x$ with itself satisfies $K(xx) \le K(x) + c$.

results.title: Pair description
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For binary strings $p$ and $q$, the pair description of $p$ and $q$ is the binary string $1^{|p|} 0 p q$, that is, $|p|$ ones, where $|p|$ is the length of $p$, then a zero, then $p$, then $q$.

results.title: Reading pair descriptions
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Write a binary string $s$ as $1^n s'$, where $n$ is the number of leading $1$s, and let $r$ be $s'$ without its first letter ($r$ is empty when $s'$ is). Let $r_1$ be the first $\min(n, |r|)$ letters of $r$ and $r_2$ the remaining ones. The pair reader maps $s$ to the concatenation $U(r_1)\,U(r_2)$, where $U$ is the universal description method, and is undefined when $U(r_1)$ or $U(r_2)$ is undefined. On a pair…

results.title: Concatenation costs at most twice the first part
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There is a natural number $c$ such that for all binary strings $x$ and $y$, the Kolmogorov complexity of their concatenation $xy$ satisfies $K(xy) \le 2K(x) + K(y) + c$.

results.title: Parent values of a node
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The values of the parents of node `k` in a full assignment `x`.

results.title: The intervention `do(X_k = a)`
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The mechanism of node `k` is replaced by the point mass at `a`, and all incoming arrows to `k` are deleted (its parent set becomes `∅`); every other node keeps its parents and its table. (The new table of `k` is the point mass on the empty parent set; the tables of the other nodes are transported along the equality of their parent sets.)

results.title: Intervention deletes the parents of the intervened node
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The parents of the intervened node are deleted.

results.title: Intervention leaves the parents of other nodes unchanged
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The parents of every other node are unchanged by the intervention.

results.title: The truncated factorization
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The truncated factorization (Pearl 2009, eq. (3.10)): after `do(X_k = a)` the joint is the product of the tables of all nodes other than `k` on assignments with `x_k = a`, and `0` elsewhere.

results.title: Intervention preserves the law of the parents
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The intervention `do(X_k = a)` does not change the law of the parents of node `k`.

results.title: Adjustment for the direct causes
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: A node's table is its conditional law given its parents
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The table of node `k` is the conditional law of `X_k` given its parents: `P(X_k = a, pa_k = z) = p_k (a | z) P(pa_k = z)`.

results.title: Adjustment for the direct causes under table positivity
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Back-door adjustment for a set of predecessors containing the parents
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: A node's table is its conditional law given a predecessor set
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a set `Z` of predecessors of `k` containing its parents, the table of `k` is its conditional law given `Z`: `P(X_k = a, Z = z) = p_k (a | z_{pa k}) P(Z = z)`.

results.title: Back-door adjustment for a set of predecessors
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Back-door adjustment for a set of predecessors containing the parents, when the table of node `k` gives the value `a` positive probability at every value of the parents.

results.title: Edge of a Bayesian network
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The edge `i → j` of the network's graph: `i` is a parent of `j`.

results.title: Descendant relation in a Bayesian network
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: `j` is a descendant of `i` (every node is its own descendant).

results.title: Adjacency in the skeleton of a Bayesian network
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: `i` and `j` are adjacent in the skeleton of the graph.

results.title: Path in the skeleton of a Bayesian network
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A path of the skeleton from `x` to `y`: a list of distinct nodes, consecutive ones adjacent, starting at `x` and ending at `y`.

results.title: Blocking at a node of a path
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The consecutive nodes `u, m, w` of a path are blocked by `Z` (Pearl 2009, Definition 1.2.3): either `m` is a collider `u → m ← w` none of whose descendants is in `Z`, or `m` is not a collider (a chain or a fork) and `m ∈ Z`.

results.title: Blocked path
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A path is blocked by `Z` if some three consecutive nodes of it are.

results.title: d-separation
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: d-separation (Pearl 1988; Pearl 2009, Definition 1.2.3): `Z` d-separates `X` from `Y` if every path between a node of `X` and a node of `Y` is blocked by `Z`.

results.title: Blocking at a node is independent of path direction
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Blocking at a node does not depend on the direction in which the path is read.

results.title: The reverse of a path is a path
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The reverse of a path from `x` to `y` is a path from `y` to `x`.

results.title: Reversal preserves blocked paths
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If a path is blocked by `Z`, so is its reverse.

results.title: Symmetry of d-separation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Symmetry of d-separation. d-separation is symmetric.

results.title: Mutilated network of a set intervention
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The network of the intervention `do(X_W = w)` with the arrows into `W` removed: every node `j ∈ W` has no parents and the point mass at `w j` as its table.

results.title: The truncated factorization for a set of nodes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: After `do(X_W = w)`, the joint is the product of the tables of the nodes outside `W` on assignments agreeing with `w` on `W`.

results.title: Descendants in the mutilated network are descendants in the original
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A descendant after removing the arrows into `W` is a descendant in `b`.

results.title: Intervened nodes descend only from themselves
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: After removing the arrows into `W`, a node of `W` is a descendant only of itself.

results.title: Assignments contradicting an intervention have probability zero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: After `do(X_k = a)`, assignments with `x k ≠ a` have probability `0`.

results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Assertion

results.title: Entailment of assertions

results.title: Substitution in an assertion

results.summary: Let $P$ be an assertion, $x$ a variable and $e$ an arithmetic expression. The assertion $P[e/x]$ holds in a state $s$ exactly when $P$ holds in the state obtained from $s$ by setting the value of $x$ to the value of $e$ in $s$.

results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For assertions $P$ and $Q$ and a command $c$, the partial-correctness Hoare triple $\lbrace P \rbrace\ c\ \lbrace Q \rbrace$ is valid when, for all states $s$ and $t$, if $s$ satisfies $P$ and executing $c$ from $s$ terminates in $t$ under the big-step semantics, then $t$ satisfies $Q$.

Then $I$ entails the weakest liberal precondition of the loop $\mathtt{while}\ b\ \mathtt{do}\ c$ with respect to $Q$.

results.caption: Definition

results.title: Total correctness implies partial correctness
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For assertions $P$, $Q$ and a command $c$, if the total-correctness Hoare triple with precondition $P$, command $c$ and postcondition $Q$ is valid, then the partial-correctness Hoare triple with the same precondition, command and postcondition is valid.

results.title: Total correctness gives a terminating small-step run
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If the total-correctness Hoare triple with precondition $P$, command $c$ and postcondition $Q$ is valid and a state $s$ satisfies $P$, then there is a state $t$ such that $c$, started in $s$, reaches $\mathtt{skip}$ with state $t$ in finitely many small steps, and $t$ satisfies $Q$.

results.title: Weakest precondition for total correctness
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a command $c$ and a postcondition $Q$, the weakest precondition $\mathrm{wp}(c, Q)$ is the assertion that holds at a state $s$ exactly when there is a terminating big-step execution of $c$ from $s$ ending in a state that satisfies $Q$.

results.title: Weakest-precondition unfolding of a while loop
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a Boolean guard $b$, a loop body $c$, a postcondition $Q$ and a state $s$, the state $s$ satisfies the total-correctness weakest precondition $\mathrm{wp}(\mathtt{while}\ b\ \mathtt{do}\ c, Q)$ if and only if either $b$ evaluates to false in $s$ and $s$ satisfies $Q$, or $b$ evaluates to true in $s$ and $s$ satisfies $\mathrm{wp}(c, \mathrm{wp}(\mathtt{while}\ b\ \mathtt{do}\ c, Q))$.

results.title: Soundness of Hoare logic for partial correctness
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every partial-correctness Hoare triple $\{P\}\,c\,\{Q\}$ that is derivable in the partial-correctness proof system is valid: for all states $s$ and $s'$, if $s$ satisfies $P$ and $c$ has a terminating big-step execution from $s$ to $s'$, then $s'$ satisfies $Q$.

results.title: Partial-correctness Hoare logic as an inference system
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Partial-correctness Hoare logic matches the denotational semantics

results.title: Counted loop runs are big-step executions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $b$ be a boolean expression, $c$ a command, $n$ a natural number and $s$, $t$ states. If the loop $\mathtt{while}\ b\ \mathtt{do}\ c$, started in $s$, exits in $t$ after exactly $n$ executions of the body $c$, then the loop $\mathtt{while}\ b\ \mathtt{do}\ c$ runs from $s$ to $t$ in the big-step semantics.

results.title: Every terminating loop run has an iteration count
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $b$ be a Boolean expression, $c$ a command and $s$, $s'$ states. If the loop $\mathtt{while}\ b\ \mathtt{do}\ c$ has a terminating big-step execution from $s$ to $s'$, then there is a natural number $n$ such that the loop, started in $s$, exits in $s'$ after exactly $n$ executions of the body $c$.

results.title: Uniqueness of the loop iteration count
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $b$ be a boolean expression, $c$ a command and $s$ a state. If the loop $\mathtt{while}\ b\ \mathtt{do}\ c$, started in $s$, exits in a state $t$ after exactly $n$ executions of the body and also exits in a state $t'$ after exactly $m$ executions of the body, then $n = m$.

results.title: Loop iteration count
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $b$ be a Boolean expression, $c$ a command and $s$ a state. If there are a natural number $n$ and a state $s'$ such that the loop $\mathtt{while}\ b\ \mathtt{do}\ c$, started in $s$, exits in $s'$ after exactly $n$ executions of the body $c$, then the iteration count of the loop from $s$ is such an $n$; otherwise it is $0$.

results.title: The iteration count of a terminating loop run
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $b$ be a Boolean expression, $c$ a command, $n$ a natural number and $s$, $s'$ states. If the loop $\mathtt{while}\ b\ \mathtt{do}\ c$, started in $s$, exits in $s'$ after exactly $n$ executions of the body $c$, then the iteration count of the loop from $s$ is $n$.

results.title: The iteration count of a nonterminating loop is zero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $b$ be a Boolean expression, $c$ a command and $s$ a state. If the loop $\mathtt{while}\ b\ \mathtt{do}\ c$ has no terminating big-step execution from $s$ to any state, then the iteration count of the loop from $s$ is $0$.

results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Precondition strengthening for total correctness
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $P$, $P'$ and $Q$ be assertions and $c$ a command. If $P$ entails $P'$ (every state satisfying $P$ satisfies $P'$) and the triple $\{P'\}\,c\,\{Q\}$ is derivable in total-correctness Hoare logic, then so is $\{P\}\,c\,\{Q\}$.

results.title: The weakest-precondition triple is derivable in total-correctness Hoare logic
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every IMP command $c$ and every assertion $Q$ (a predicate on states), the triple $\{\mathrm{wp}(c, Q)\}\,c\,\{Q\}$ is derivable in the total-correctness Hoare logic. Here $\mathrm{wp}(c, Q)$ is the semantic weakest precondition: it holds in a state $s$ exactly when there is a terminating execution of $c$ from $s$ ending in a state satisfying $Q$.

results.title: Total-correctness Hoare logic is relatively complete
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all assertions $P$ and $Q$ and every command $c$, if the total-correctness Hoare triple $\{P\}\,c\,\{Q\}$ is valid, then it is derivable in total-correctness Hoare logic.

results.title: Total-correctness derivations give partial-correctness derivations
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all assertions $P$ and $Q$ and every command $c$, if the triple with precondition $P$, command $c$ and postcondition $Q$ is derivable in total-correctness Hoare logic, then it is derivable in partial-correctness Hoare logic.

results.title: Soundness and relative completeness of total-correctness Hoare logic
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all assertions $P$, $Q$ (predicates on states) and every IMP command $c$, the triple $\{P\}\,c\,\{Q\}$ is derivable in the total-correctness Hoare logic if and only if it is totally valid.

results.title: Total-correctness Hoare logic is sound and complete for the denotational semantics
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all assertions $P$, $Q$ (predicates on states) and every IMP command $c$, the triple $\{P\}\,c\,\{Q\}$ is derivable in the total-correctness Hoare logic if and only if for every state $s$ satisfying $P$ there is a state $s'$ such that $(s, s')$ lies in the relational denotation of $c$ and $s'$ satisfies $Q$.

results.title: Hoare triples
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A Hoare triple $\{P\}\,c\,\{Q\}$ consists of a precondition $P$ and a postcondition $Q$, both assertions (predicates on states), and an IMP command $c$. It is the judgement form of both the partial-correctness and the total-correctness Hoare logic.

results.title: Total-correctness tag for Hoare triples
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: An empty type used only as a label: derivability of Hoare triples in the total-correctness Hoare logic is registered as an inference system under this tag, while partial-correctness derivability is the default inference system on Hoare triples.

results.title: Derivability in the default inference system on Hoare triples is validity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every Hoare triple $\{P\}\,c\,\{Q\}$, the triple is derivable in the default inference system on Hoare triples, which is partial-correctness Hoare logic, if and only if it is valid for partial correctness.

results.title: Total-correctness Hoare logic as an inference system
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A Hoare triple, given by a precondition $P$, a command $c$ and a postcondition $Q$, is derivable in the inference system on Hoare triples tagged total correctness, which is total-correctness Hoare logic, if and only if it is valid for total correctness.
